concerns: Assay sensitivity and capture-compatibility for low-biomass lavage/CSF samples is a critical dependency; existing large-animal negative biodistribution (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution) highlights risk of false negatives and species barriers.

Feasibility of producing a true particle-count-matched but capture-depleted comparator is uncertain and not addressed by the cited evidence; practical inability to generate this comparator would weaken the falsification criterion.

Reliance on short-interval ex vivo cytokine readouts as a proxy for in vivo neuroimmune modulation is an inference not directly validated by the canonical studies (rodent efficacy reports show outcome improvements but do not link those outcomes to capture-verified intact EV exposure).

Proposal appropriately frames rodent efficacy as insufficient to claim intact-EV exposure in larger species and does not misattribute literature as SGL-001 experimental data; ensure all future internal experimental results are not conflated with published preclinical findings when claiming product-specific evidence.
conclusion: Supported with important evidence gaps. The proposal correctly cites rodent intranasal preclinical bioactivity (ev-zhuang-2011, ev-kodali-2017, ev-hermann-2023) and appropriately invokes MISEV2023 quality/characterization recommendations (ev-misev2023-quality-framework). It also properly acknowledges a large-animal negative biodistribution result that limits cross-species generalizability (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution). The orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridging experiment proposed is a reasonable and necessary next step; however, the specific causal claim that a capture-positive, membrane-protected fraction will predict short-interval ex vivo CNS cytokine modulation is not directly supported by the supplied canonical evidence and therefore remains unproven.
evidence_gap: No canonical evidence demonstrates that orthogonally verified, capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive EVs recovered from short-interval nasal/CSF/olfactory-mucosa samples causally predict an ex vivo cytokine-modulatory effect after intranasal dosing. In particular, there is no published matched in vivo→ex vivo experiment comparing capture-positive versus membrane-disrupted and capture-depleted, particle-count-matched arms as proposed.
